title: Gibeon and the Gibeonites
lead: A Hivite town north of Jerusalem whose people tricked Joshua into a treaty and became servants at the sanctuary. Later the great high place where Solomon asked for wisdom (Joshua 9–10; 2 Samuel 21; 1 Kings 3).

sections.b: The Gibeonites won a sworn treaty by pretending to come from far away, and were made to cut wood and carry water for the house of God (Joshua 9). Israel defended them against five kings, the battle of the long day (Joshua 10). Gibeon was given to Benjamin as a priests' town (Joshua 18:25; Joshua 21:17). At the pool of Gibeon the men of David and Ishbosheth fought (2 Samuel 2:12–17). Saul's attack on the Gibeonites brought a famine in David's reign, ended only when seven of Saul's descendants were handed over (2 Samuel 21:1–14). Solomon worshiped at "the great high place" of Gibeon and asked for wisdom there (1 Kings 3:4–15). Gibeonites helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall after the exile (Nehemiah 3:7).
